title: The file area flashes a skeleton between keystrokes at zero results and shows the old rows under the new column when switching Name/Contents
problem: `run_search` sets `self.searching = true` and notifies before the debounce even starts (src/finder/mod.rs:1388-1395). `render_content` shows the centered message only when `rows.is_empty() && !self.searching` (mod.rs:3236) and otherwise falls through to `render_skeleton` for empty rows (3267-3268). So once a query has no results, every further keystroke swaps 'No Results' for 14 skeleton bars for at least 50 ms and back again. The indexing retry does the same every 600 ms or less (`run_search(false)` at mod.rs:1451-1455), so 'Indexing...' blinks against the skeleton while the index builds. Separately, `set_search_contents` flips the mode and re-runs (mod.rs:1478-1483) but the rows are replaced only when the response lands (1428-1430), while the column title follows the flag immediately (`parent_column_title`, src/finder/list.rs:247-260): for up to the contents time limit (5 s default) the list shows name-search rows with folder paths under a 'Match' header, or match lines under 'Folder' going the other way, with only the 11-pt status-bar spinner (src/finder/bars.rs:406-408) saying anything is pending. The first keystroke of a search has the same shape: `is_searching()` flips at once, so the folder's own rows are drawn as results with a Folder column until the first response.
proposal: src/finder/mod.rs: (1) in `render_content`, show the skeleton only while no response has arrived for this search (`self.searching && self.search_stats.is_none()`); once `search_stats` is `Some`, keep the message branch for empty rows while a newer request runs, with title 'No Results' for name search and 'Searching...' for a contents search still in flight. (2) Add a small `drop_stale_results(cx)` (`results.clear(); search_stats = None; selection.clear(); rebuild_rows(cx)`) and call it in `set_search_contents` before `run_search`, and in `set_query`'s `!was_searching` branch (1340-1346), so rows that belong to another kind of list are replaced by the skeleton until the first answer. Leave `set_scope`/`set_kind` and plain query edits as they are (same kind of rows, no flash). Give the skeleton rows and the message title `.test_support()` ids so tests can see which one is drawn.
original_test_plan: Headless UI tests using `ui.window(..)` without `settle` to look at the in-flight frame: (a) `ui.click("search")`, `ui.type_text("zzzz")` (settled, zero results), then `ui.window(|w, cx| w.input("q", cx))` and assert `!ui.exists(("sk-row", 0usize))` and that the message title is still present (fails today). (b) `set_query("atlas")` settled, then `ui.window(|_, cx| view.update(cx, |f, cx| f.set_search_contents(true, cx)))` unsettled and assert `ui.names().is_empty()`; after `ui.settle()` assert every row's `detail` starts with a line number.
original_risks: Clearing rows at the first keystroke trades a flash of relabelled folder rows for a brief skeleton; if that reads worse in practice, keep only the Name/Contents part. `search_stats` must still be reset to `None` when a search ends (it is, mod.rs:1334) or the skeleton would never show for the next search. Touches the same `render_content` branch as empty-state-messages and collapsed-groups-empty-view.

verifier.claim_check:
Every part of the described behaviour is true; nothing handles it today, and neither CHANGELOG.md nor docs/manual.md covers it.

- **Zero-result flash:** `run_search` sets `searching = true` and notifies before the 50 ms debounce timer (src/finder/mod.rs:1388-1395). `render_content` shows the message only when `rows.is_empty() && !self.loading && !self.searching` (mod.rs:3236), and empty rows otherwise fall to `render_skeleton` (mod.rs:3267-3268). A search view is never Columns (`effective_view`, mod.rs:854-861), so the Columns branch does not intervene. At zero results each keystroke therefore draws 14 bars (list) or 18 tiles (icons/gallery) for at least 50 ms plus search time. CHANGELOG.md:81 puts a name search at 25-35 ms on a large index.
- **Indexing blink:** the retry calls `run_search(false)` at mod.rs:1451-1455 after at most 24 x 25 ms. `searching` is true only for the search itself there, so "Indexing…" blinks against the skeleton intermittently rather than on every retry.
- **Name/Contents switch:** `set_search_contents` (mod.rs:1478-1483) flips the flag and re-runs; rows are replaced only at mod.rs:1428-1430. The header and cell style follow the flag at once (`parent_column_shows_match` / `parent_column_title`, src/finder/list.rs:247-260; cell at src/finder/views.rs:958-972). The content time limit defaults to 5 s (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:378). The only pending cue is the status-bar spinner (src/finder/bars.rs:406-408).
- **First keystroke:** `set_query`'s `!was_searching` branch (mod.rs:1340-1346) clears the selection but not the rows, so the folder's rows are drawn with a Folder column (`Row::new` fills `detail` with the parent folder, mod.rs:114-115).
- **Worse than the candidate states:** `search_contents` is never reset when a search ends (only written at mod.rs:1480 and src/finder/filter.rs:227). After one Contents search, the first keystroke of any later search shows folder rows under "Match" for up to the time limit. A Smart Folder saved with Contents does the same.

No test pins this: tests/*.rs has no match for `sk-row`, `sk-tile`, "No Results" or "Indexing". docs/manual.md:120-128 lists the empty-area messages and has no "Searching…" row.
verifier.implementation_notes:
Keep the proposal's two parts, with these corrections.

**1. `render_content` (src/finder/mod.rs:3236-3268)**
- Draw the skeleton for empty rows only when `self.loading`, or when `self.searching` and either `search_stats.is_none()` or the last answer came from a partial index that has since finished (`stats.indexing && self.indexing_progress().is_none()`).
- The second condition is a correction. `poll_index_status` (mod.rs:1503-1511) updates `index_status` and calls `run_search(false)` in the same update. With the proposal as written, "Indexing…" would become a false "No Results" for the length of that search, just before results appear.
- Otherwise keep the message while a newer request runs. Title order: `indexing_progress()` is `Some` gives "Indexing…"; `self.searching && self.search_contents` gives "Searching…"; else "No Results".

**2. `drop_stale_results(cx)`**
- Body as proposed: `results.clear(); search_stats = None; selection.clear(); rebuild_rows(cx)`.
- Go through `rebuild_rows`, not `rows.clear()`: `groups`, `icon_layout`, the marquee and `unfiltered_len` are derived there (mod.rs:1260-1273, src/finder/groups.rs:129-144).
- Call it in `set_query`'s `!was_searching` branch (mod.rs:1340). Do it for name searches too, because `search_contents` is sticky; this also covers `open_smart_folder` and `open_request`.
- Call it in `set_search_contents`, guarded by `self.is_searching()`, so a call outside a search cannot clear a folder's selection.
- Leave `set_scope`, `set_kind` and plain query edits alone.

**3. Filter pitfall (src/finder/filter.rs:96-109)**
- With a Nushell filter on, `rebuild_rows` on empty rows starts `start_filter([])`. That finishes at once with `filter_keep = Some(empty)`, which hides the first real results behind "No Results" until the real `nu` run ends.
- Today `open_smart_folder` shows the unfiltered rows in that window, because `set_filter` has just reset `filter_keep` to `None`.
- Fix: return early from `apply_filter_to` when `rows.is_empty()`.

**4. Test ids**
- The default view is Icons (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:295), so the skeleton there is `sk-tile`, not `sk-row`. Put `.id("skeleton").test_support()` on the container in both arms of `render_skeleton` (src/finder/views.rs:1319-1357).
- In `render_message` (mod.rs:3394) give the title `.id("message-title").aria_label(title)` and `.test_support()`, as `status-text` does at src/finder/bars.rs:392-396. `label()` reads the aria label, not drawn text.
- Add `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn search_in_flight_for_test(&self) -> bool` next to `rows_for_test` (mod.rs:683), so tests can prove the request is still pending.

**5. Docs**
- Add a "Searching…" row to the table at docs/manual.md:120-128.
- Add a Fixed entry under [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md.
verifier.test_plan:
Put the tests in tests/controls.rs, in the search section near line 301, using the headless harness in tests/common/mod.rs.

**Harness addition:** `Ui::type_text_without_settling(text)` beside `click_without_settling` (common/mod.rs:333), calling `self.window(|w, cx| w.input(text, cx))`. common/mod.rs already imports `TestWindowExt`. `InputEvent::Change` is emitted synchronously and flushed when the window update returns, and nothing spawned runs until `settle()`. `click_without_settling` already relies on this at controls.rs:671-678.

**(a) No skeleton between keystrokes at zero results**
- `Fixture::new`, `Ui::open`, `ui.click("search")`, `ui.type_text("qqzzqqzz")`.
- Assert `ui.names().is_empty()` and `ui.snapshot("message-title").label() == Some("No Results")`.
- `ui.type_text_without_settling("q")`, then assert `ui.read(|f| f.search_in_flight_for_test())`.
- Assert `!ui.exists("skeleton")` and that the title is still "No Results". This fails today.
- `ui.settle()`.

**(b) Name to Contents drops the name rows**
- `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.set_query("atlas".into(), true, cx))`, then `ui.click_without_settling("by-contents")`.
- Assert `ui.names().is_empty()` and `ui.exists("skeleton")`. This fails today.
- After `ui.settle()`, assert every `rows_for_test()` row's `detail` starts with "1: ". The fixture's Project Atlas.txt contains "atlas".

**(c) First keystroke**
- `ui.click("search")`, `ui.type_text_without_settling("a")`.
- Assert `ui.names().is_empty()` and `ui.exists("skeleton")`; after `ui.settle()`, names are non-empty.

**(d) Contents search in flight at zero rows**
- In Contents mode, type a no-match query and settle, then type one more key unsettled.
- Assert the title label is "Searching…".

**Not covered:** the indexing blink needs a scanning index, which the harness waits out (`wait_ready` in `Ui::open_with`). It goes through the same branch as (a).

**Regression checks:** re-run `scope_bar_controls` (controls.rs:361), `search_field_typing_escape_and_down_arrow` (controls.rs:304), `searches_by_name_and_returns_to_browsing` (tests/finder.rs:67) and the filter and Smart Folder test (controls.rs:1421-1487, needs `nu`). All of them settle before asserting, so their expected end states are unchanged.
verifier.risks:
- **Return while the first answer is pending:** the `PressEnter` handler (mod.rs:1308-1317) checks `self.rows` synchronously. With rows dropped on the first keystroke or on a Name/Contents switch, Return pressed before the first answer no longer moves focus into the list. Today it moves focus onto stale rows and selects one that the response then remaps away. This is a small change to the documented "Return … moves into the results" (docs/manual.md:324) in a window of about 80 ms for names and up to 5 s for contents.
- **First keystroke of a name search:** it now shows a skeleton for roughly 55-85 ms instead of relabelled folder rows. This is a matter of taste, but it is needed because the Contents mode is sticky.
- **Contents to Name:** a one-or-two-frame skeleton appears on the switch.
- **Fast contents search at zero results:** the title still flips between "No Results" and "Searching…" per keystroke. This is milder than the skeleton swap and is the price of not claiming "No Results" during a 5 s grep.
- **Filter guard:** the `rows.is_empty()` early return leaves `filter_source` and `filter_keep` from the previous list in place while a list is empty. That matches the existing stale-keep behaviour, but the Smart Folder test should confirm it.
- **Two panes:** `message-title` is not unique when both split panes show a message, so tests there must scope the lookup.
- **Merge conflicts:** the change touches the same `render_content` branch as the empty-state-messages and collapsed-groups-empty-view candidates.

orchestrator_notes: The improvement 'search-enter-before-results' (Return and Down pressed before results arrive) is meant to land before this one. Check the trunk for it first and make sure the two work together: dropping rows early must not break Return or Down pressed while the first answer is pending.
